Is there an official name for the protocol? In the release note entry it's "Microsoft Cluster Remote Control Protocol (RCP)", in the file header it's "Microsoft Cluster Heartbeat Route Control Protocol (RCP)" and here it's "RCP Protocol". Note that

* Something called "[rcp](http://manpages.ubuntu.com/manpages/bionic/man1/netkit-rcp.1.html)" has been around a long time in the Unix world, although it's been historical / obsolete for many years.

* The MS NLB dissector prefixes a lot of its naming, including its filter names and filename with "MS" or "ms" as appropriate.

This dissector is based on a Network Monitor parser that was deprecated a few years ago.

Unfortunately, archive.org doesn't have a backup of the download: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/download/details.aspx?id=53671&751be11f-ede8-5a0c-058c-2ee190a24fa6=True

In the .npl parser the protocol is denoted just as Route Control Protocol and abbreviated rcp. But from what you have said it may be more appropriate to have the parser named ms-rcp.
